title: Chrome Browser Extension (Manifest V3)
description: Step-by-step workflow for designing, building, and publishing a production-ready Chrome Extension using Manifest V3, Vite, and React.

steps.title: Extension Concept & Browser Context
steps.goal: Define the extension category, user trigger context, and core browser interaction model.
steps.expectedOutput: Extension type, trigger context (page action vs global), and core permissions needed.
steps.prompt:
I am building a Chrome Extension called "{{project.name}}".
The concept is: {{project.idea}}.
My experience level is {{project.experienceLevel}}.

1. Classify the extension type: page action (active on specific sites), browser action (global toolbar button), or devtools panel.
2. Define the trigger context: when does the user interact? (clicking icon, right-click context menu, keyboard shortcut, page load).
3. List the Chrome APIs and permissions needed (e.g. `tabs`, `storage`, `activeTab`, `scripting`, `webRequest`, `notifications`).
4. Identify any content security policy constraints or cross-origin restrictions to plan around.

steps.title: MVP Feature Scope & UI Surface Map
steps.goal: Map out the popup UI, options page, and content script injection points for V1.
steps.expectedOutput: List of UI surfaces (popup, options, content script overlay), core features, and explicit non-goals.
steps.prompt:
Scope the MVP for "{{project.name}}" (extension type: {{decisions.extensionType}}, triggers: {{decisions.triggerContext}}):
1. Map the UI surfaces: popup (dimensions, key actions), options page (settings), any content script overlay injected into pages.
2. List 3-5 MVP features with clear user stories.
3. Define what data is stored locally (chrome.storage.local vs chrome.storage.sync).
4. List 5 explicit V1 non-goals.
5. Identify any sites where the extension will primarily be used and any site-specific permissions needed.

steps.title: Build Tooling & Framework Selection
steps.goal: Select Vite, framework (React/Vanilla), and extension-specific bundling configuration.
steps.expectedOutput: Vite + React + TypeScript setup with chrome-extension rollup/vite plugin configuration.
steps.prompt:
Select the build stack for "{{project.name}}" Chrome Extension with UI surfaces: {{decisions.uiSurfaces}}:
1. Build tool: Vite with `@crxjs/vite-plugin` (recommended) or webpack with `webpack-extension-manifest-plugin`.
2. UI framework: React 18 + TypeScript (for complex UI) or Vanilla JS/TS (for lightweight extensions).
3. Styling: Tailwind CSS with preflight reset scoped to extension shadow DOM.
4. State management: Zustand or jotai for shared state between popup and content scripts via chrome.storage.
5. Testing: Vitest for unit tests, Playwright for E2E tests of the popup UI.
6. Provide the complete project initialization commands.

steps.title: Manifest V3 Configuration
steps.goal: Define the complete manifest.json with all required fields, permissions, and entry points.
steps.expectedOutput: Complete manifest.json with action, background service worker, content scripts, permissions, and web_accessible_resources.
steps.prompt:
Write the complete Manifest V3 `manifest.json` for "{{project.name}}" (type: {{decisions.extensionType}}, surfaces: {{decisions.uiSurfaces}}):
1. Required fields: manifest_version (3), name, version, description.
2. `action` block: popup path, default icon set (16, 32, 48, 128px).
3. `background.service_worker` path and `type: module`.
4. `content_scripts`: matches (URL patterns), js/css files, run_at timing.
5. `permissions` array (only request the minimum required).
6. `host_permissions` for any external APIs.
7. `web_accessible_resources` for any assets accessed from content scripts.
8. `commands` for keyboard shortcuts.
9. `options_page` or `options_ui` path.

steps.title: Background Service Worker
steps.goal: Implement the service worker for extension lifecycle events, message routing, and API calls.
steps.expectedOutput: Service worker handling install, message routing, context menu registration, and alarm/scheduled tasks.
steps.prompt:
Implement the background service worker for "{{project.name}}":
1. `onInstalled` handler: set default storage values and create context menus.
2. Message listener: `chrome.runtime.onMessage` routing messages from popup and content scripts.
3. Context menu registration and handler.
4. `chrome.alarms` setup for any scheduled background tasks.
5. Badge text/color updates on toolbar icon based on state.
6. Any external API calls (service workers cannot use XMLHttpRequest, must use fetch).
7. Error handling and logging pattern for service worker context.

steps.title: Content Script & Page DOM Injection
steps.goal: Implement content scripts that safely interact with host page DOM and communicate with the service worker.
steps.expectedOutput: Content script with isolated shadow DOM overlay, message passing to background, and page DOM manipulation.
steps.prompt:
Implement the content script for "{{project.name}}":
1. Initialize content script safely: check if already injected using a sentinel element.
2. Create an isolated shadow DOM root to inject React UI without conflicting with host page styles.
3. `chrome.runtime.sendMessage` to communicate with the background service worker.
4. `chrome.runtime.onMessage` listener to receive commands from popup or background.
5. DOM observation using `MutationObserver` if the extension needs to react to page content changes.
6. Clean teardown function to remove the overlay when the extension is disabled.

steps.title: Popup UI Components & Storage Integration
steps.goal: Build the extension popup with React, connected to chrome.storage for persistent settings and state.
steps.expectedOutput: Popup React app with chrome.storage hooks, main feature UI, and settings toggle.
steps.prompt:
Build the popup UI for "{{project.name}}" using {{decisions.uiFramework}}:
1. `src/hooks/useStorage.ts` — Custom hook wrapping `chrome.storage.sync.get/set` with React state sync.
2. Main popup App component (max 400x600px) with the primary feature UI.
3. Enable/disable toggle persisted to chrome.storage.
4. Status indicator showing current page compatibility.
5. Quick action buttons sending messages to content script via `chrome.tabs.sendMessage`.
6. Loading and error states for async storage operations.
7. Link to open options page.

steps.title: Options Page & User Settings
steps.goal: Build a full-page settings UI allowing users to configure extension behavior and manage stored data.
steps.expectedOutput: Options page with categorized settings, form validation, import/export data, and reset to defaults.
steps.prompt:
Build the options page for "{{project.name}}":
1. Full-page React app with tabbed settings categories.
2. Settings form with validation, auto-save on change, and success/error toast feedback.
3. Data management section: export all stored data as JSON, import from JSON file, reset to defaults.
4. Whitelist/blacklist URL pattern editor (if applicable).
5. Keyboard shortcut configuration display (linking to chrome://extensions/shortcuts).
6. About section showing version, links to privacy policy and support.

steps.title: Storage Architecture & Message Passing Protocol
steps.goal: Define the chrome.storage schema, message type system, and cross-context communication patterns.
steps.expectedOutput: TypeScript storage schema, typed message union types, and message passing utility functions.
steps.prompt:
Design the data and messaging layer for "{{project.name}}":
1. `src/types/storage.ts` — TypeScript interface defining all chrome.storage.sync and chrome.storage.local schemas.
2. `src/types/messages.ts` — Discriminated union type for all message types between popup, content, and background.
3. `src/lib/storage.ts` — Type-safe wrappers for chrome.storage get/set/remove with error handling.
4. `src/lib/messaging.ts` — Type-safe `sendMessage` and `onMessage` utilities.
5. Storage migration pattern for handling schema changes between extension versions.

steps.title: Icons, Screenshots & Promo Assets
steps.goal: Create and optimize all required extension icons and Chrome Web Store promotional assets.
steps.expectedOutput: Icon generation script, store screenshot templates, and promo tile specifications.
steps.prompt:
Prepare visual assets for "{{project.name}}":
1. Icon requirements: 16x16, 32x32, 48x48, 128x128 PNG icons (main icon and disabled/inactive variant).
2. Script to auto-generate icon sizes from a single SVG source using `sharp` or `Inkscape CLI`.
3. Chrome Web Store screenshots: 1280x800 or 640x400 PNG format, 5 screenshots recommended.
4. Promo tiles: small (440x280), large (920x680), and marquee (1400x560) for featured placement.
5. Screenshot content recommendations: show the extension in action on a real website.

steps.title: Testing: Unit, Integration & Playwright E2E
steps.goal: Test message passing, storage logic, popup rendering, and end-to-end flows in a real browser.
steps.expectedOutput: Vitest unit tests for utilities, JSDOM component tests for popup, and Playwright E2E with extension loading.
steps.prompt:
Write tests for "{{project.name}}":
1. Vitest unit tests for `lib/storage.ts` and `lib/messaging.ts` with chrome API mocks.
2. React Testing Library tests for the popup App component (mocking chrome storage responses).
3. Playwright E2E test loading the unpacked extension:
   a. Load extension from `dist/` directory using `--load-extension` flag.
   b. Navigate to a test page, click the extension icon, verify popup opens correctly.
   c. Interact with the popup and verify the content script receives the message.
4. Mock chrome APIs for unit tests using `jest-chrome` or `vitest-chrome`.

steps.title: Chrome Web Store Publication & CI/CD
steps.goal: Package, submit, and automate the publishing of the extension to the Chrome Web Store.
steps.expectedOutput: Store listing configuration, automated build + publish GitHub Actions workflow, and review guidelines.
steps.prompt:
Publish "{{project.name}}" to the Chrome Web Store:
1. `npm run build` output verification: confirm `dist/manifest.json` is valid and all assets are present.
2. Chrome Web Store Developer Dashboard setup: create a new item, fill in name, description (132 chars), and upload screenshots.
3. Privacy policy requirements: what data is collected, where it's stored, disclosure for host permissions.
4. `chrome-webstore-upload` GitHub Action to automate publishing on git tag push:
   - Build the extension.
   - Upload to Web Store using OAuth refresh token.
   - Submit for review.
5. Versioning strategy: bump `version` in `manifest.json` and `package.json` together using a release script.
6. Common rejection reasons to avoid: excessive permissions, vague descriptions, missing privacy policy.
